hypothesis: Partitioned owner scheduler on: the CPU control at baseline operating points returns normally with exact coverage and per-core wake and lock timing comparable to baseline 1793566204991504422-8a47d893
note: The first recorded fault is the initial stack-pair store in FreeRTOS_Yield after selecting SP_EL0. SP_EL0 holds an address in the read-only code block because no task context had been restored on core 0: the first board task changed its core affinity before the scheduler started and the owner scheduler yielded. The virtual OS board reproduces the fault with the same ESR. The watchdog ends launch; the port is quarantined and the runner records DRAM lost after a user replug.

hypothesis: Owner scheduler with the pre-start yield refused (upstream tasks.c:3073 behaviour, QEMU SP_EL0 reproduction): the unchanged CPU control at baseline operating points returns normally with exact coverage and per-core wake and lock timing comparable to baseline 1793566204991504422-8a47d893.
note: Normal ROM return; coverage, metadata and wake counts match the expectation. Only the 25 us IRQ-masked budget fails, on cores 0, 2 and 3: the maxima are in ssKernelCommand (cores 0 and 2, outside the workload phases) and vTaskEnterCritical (core 3, workload). Selector global locks are not counted separately on the board.

hypothesis: Owner scheduler with writer-grouped cache lines and single-pass pending scans: the unchanged CPU control at baseline operating points returns normally and every interrupt-masked span stays within 25 us; compare with entry 1793588341441359431-9f76aac0.
note: Normal ROM return; coverage, metadata and wake counts match. Only the 25 us masked budget fails: core 3 in the workload (31.8 us) and the end-of-run task suspension on cores 1, 3 and 5 (32 to 47 us), which moves between cores from run to run. Wake distributions equal the previous run.

hypothesis: PMU capture of the owner-scheduler CPU control at the baseline operating points: the longest interrupt-masked spans in the measured phases retire at most 1500 instructions and, when longer than 15 us, show at least 100 L1D refills; counters are read only.
note: Normal ROM return with the PMU tail. The prediction fails: workload spans retire 770 to 2100 instructions (kernel entries up to 3560 in setup) and show 21 to 40 L1D refills, not 100, so the 17 to 30 us spans run at 25 to 50 cycles per instruction without refill counts that explain them. Barrier and far-atomic stalls against the load tasks stores are the next candidates.

hypothesis: Stall-event capture of the owner-scheduler CPU control: inside masked spans over 15 us, STALL_BACKEND is at least 70 percent of the cycles, MEM_ACCESS at most 700 and L1D refills at most 60; counters are read only.
note: Prediction holds for the busy-phase spans: STALL_BACKEND is 59 to 98 percent of cycles (core 3 below 70), MEM_ACCESS is 441 to 619 and L1D refills 23 to 38. It does not separate barrier cycles from dependent misses under saturated DRAM: a service entry with two DSB SY and 35 refills stalls 33000 cycles, 0.5 us per refill.
